method_notes: rule_file_sha256 is SHA-256 over the exact bytes of each research/readiness/type-rules/TR-*.json at review time. A file changed after this review is not covered by it.

For the 20 files with review_round 2, every string in quoted_parts (and in additional_exemplars[].quoted_parts, checked against that exemplar's own source.text_path) was checked as an exact substring of the UTF-8 text at source.text_path. Each occurs exactly once, at the recorded spans or char offsets. quoted_clause equals the single part or the parts joined. SHA-256 of each text file's UTF-8 text (and of its raw bytes) equals source.text_sha256. All 21 quote and hash checks passed.
Each exemplar text was read in full to judge whether the quote is the order's own operative text, whether its boundaries are sensible, and whether the order is a true member of the type.

Round-1 required_changes, factual_problems and missing_outliers were compared item by item with the revised files, and with REVISIONS in jobs/x1-class-engine/type_rules_spec.py. Git history was not used.

Legal propositions newly added or changed were checked by web search where noted in each item's notes; points given from memory are marked 'verify'. Two errors came from round 1's own wording and are corrected here: the scope of the FPA s.24 'until otherwise directed' clause, and the 'November 1921' treaty dates.

TR-CLOSING-MOURNING and TR-WATER-RESERVE: file sha256 recomputed, equal to the round-1 hash; round-1 decision carried (carried_from_round_1: true). TR-STOCK-DRIVEWAY is withdrawn and not reviewed. Its orders fall under TR-LAND-WITHDRAWAL, whose stock-driveway outlier was reviewed.

This is an independent AI review of research PATTERNS. It is not human certification. It decides no order, fills no claim field, changes no status, and leaves the count of human-certified whole-lifecycle dossiers at 0. Rules marked approve_with_required_changes are not frozen until they are revised and reviewed again (new file hash).

Common remaining weaknesses: exceptions_savings.reviewed is false and leads is empty in every rule; three rules have duplicate outlier entries; several quotes still open or close mid-sentence (recommended fixes in notes).

new_problems: ending_pattern says EO 5888's authority is 'a candidate to have ended with Prohibition's repeal in 1933'. That is inaccurate for the Canal Zone. The 21st Amendment did not repeal federal law for a federal territory. The provision EO 5888 rests on (NPA s.20 as amended by the Act of July 5, 1932, ch. 428, 47 Stat. 579; codified 27 U.S.C. 63) was repealed by the Act of June 19, 1934, ch. 657, s.3, 48 Stat. 1116. Section 1 of that Act gave the President new authority to regulate liquor in the Canal Zone (27 U.S.C. 63a, later 48 U.S.C. 1314b; repealed 1949, 63 Stat. 597). Round 1 had said '21st Amendment ... and later repeal legislation', and the revision dropped the second half.
required_changes: Replace 'with Prohibition's repeal in 1933' with: the statutory proviso was repealed by the Act of June 19, 1934 (ch. 657, s.3, 48 Stat. 1116). That date is the candidate authority-lapse end. The same Act's s.1 gave a new liquor-regulation authority, so check whether a successor order replaced EO 5888. The 21st Amendment (Dec. 5, 1933) did not by itself end federal law in the Canal Zone.

The rule is split into (a) trust-period extensions, with a new exemplar (EO 2747, Prairie Band Pottawatomi, a 10-year extension under the Act of Feb. 8, 1887; Wikisource mirror), and (b) reservation and boundary orders, with EO 2550 as an additional exemplar re-cut to end at 'existing valid rights in and to the same.' I appendix, which says the Act of June 15, 1935 (49 Stat. 378) reimposed trust restrictions that expired between June 18, 1934 and Dec. 31, 1936 on reservations not under the IRA. The exemplar is replaced by EO 3297 (June 30, 1920; Wikisource mirror). It is a Pickett Act temporary withdrawal pending examination for a national monument, so the order itself withdraws land. The quote runs from 'Under the provisions' to the purpose clause; it is exact and the hash is verified. The FLPMA savings note is correct. Disposal (patent or sale) is added as a per-tract end, and all three missing outliers were added. The stock-driveway fold-in is reasonable. Recommended (verify): s.10 of the Stock-Raising Homestead Act (39 Stat. 862, 865) lets water holes be reserved under the Pickett Act and lets the Secretary of the Interior withdraw driveway access lands. A presidential stock-driveway order may therefore rest on the Pickett Act, so the agent should record the authority the order itself cites rather than assume s.10.

unaddressed: Round 1 asked for 'a numbered Power Site Reserve order'. The new exemplar, EO 6205, is Reservoir Site Reserve No. 19 (East Fork Deschutes, Oregon). It is a Pickett Act withdrawal 'reserved for reservoir sites', which fits the rule's title but not the power-site half of the rule, and that half is the one the new FPA s.24 text addresses.
new_problems: The FPA s.24 statement is too broad. 16 U.S.C. 818's 'until otherwise directed by the Commission or by Congress' applies to lands included in a proposed project from the date an application is filed, not to every executive-order power-site reserve. For lands 'reserved or classified as power sites', s.24 provides that they may be opened to entry on a Commission determination, subject to a reserved right of re-entry for power purposes. The wording came from round 1's own required change and is corrected here.
Duplicate outlier: the 'order itself is a restoration' condition appears twice.
required_changes: Rewrite the FPA s.24 sentences in ending_pattern and exceptions_savings as follows. Lands within a filed project application are reserved from the filing date 'until otherwise directed by the Commission or by Congress'. Lands reserved or classified as power sites (including by executive order) may be opened to entry only on a Commission determination, subject to a reserved right of re-entry. Whether s.24 applies to a given reserve (for example a reservoir site reserve made for irrigation) must be shown from the order and FPC or FERC records.

Either add a numbered Power Site Reserve exemplar (as additional_exemplars), or say expressly that the exemplar is a reservoir site reserve and that the s.24 constraint applies only where the lands are reserved or classified for power purposes.
